evidence: the methods state that where prior experimental data exist the synthetic data is constructed based on, for example, Tabular GAN (Xu et al. 2019), or statistical associations such as Bayesian network forward simulation, and that quality is judged by comparing the marginal and joint distributions of the synthetic and experimental data; step 1 of the procedure, simulating future datasets, states that the authors approximated the true data generating process with Tabular GAN (Xu et al. 2019), trained on historical observational experimental data, preprocessing and training with default hyperparameters as described in Ashrapov (2020), after which N new samples were drawn. The named implementation is Ashrapov's tabgan library rather than sdv-dev's CTGAN, so no SDV code runs even though the method is credited to Xu et al. and is load-bearing for the paper's simulation step. This entry absorbs the arXiv preprint of the same work (2210.13423, Mohammad-Taheri et al.), which was separately curated in shard 70 as paper-experimental-design-biomolecular-2022 at api_user importance 3 and has been removed as a duplicate. The two readings rested on the same fact — the preprint entry's own evidence also recorded the Ashrapov preprocessing — so the disagreement was over whether running a third-party reimplementation counts as running SDV, which is the question carried on this entry's `needs`

summary: Synthesises a mobility database in two parts, separating who the travellers are from where they go, because the joint distribution of person attributes and trip chains is too complex to learn at once; a bipartite assignment then pairs each synthetic individual with a plausible trajectory. CTGAN is the population generator: it is trained on the person table and credited with generating tabular data and learning joint distributions, with its PacGAN discriminator preventing mode collapse, while activity locations are encoded as continuous rather than discrete variables specifically to stay within CTGAN's memory behaviour, and its inability to express hierarchical trip structure is the stated reason a separate recurrent model handles the trajectories.
evidence: the model section states that the Conditional Tabular GAN differs from other GAN models in its ability to generate tabular data and learn joint distributions, and that the paper makes use of the CTGAN model to synthesize the population; the same section notes CTGAN includes the PacGAN framework to prevent mode collapse and that it has difficulty generating realistic trip distributions because it does not support hierarchical tables; the preprocessing section encodes activity locations as continuous variables because discrete zone variables cause memory issues within the CTGAN framework; the sampling section states the authors sample synthetic population and location datasets separately after training CTGAN and RNN models, and that the CTGAN and RNN components include layer, batch and epoch size parameters. This entry absorbs the arXiv preprint of the same work (2211.07369, Arkangil et al.), curated separately in shard 59 as paper-population-mobility-gan-2022 and removed as a duplicate; both readings independently reached api_user importance 4, and the fuller evidence above comes from the preprint record
